definition: Google Research (also known as Research at Google) is the research division of Google, a subsidiary of Alphabet Inc..
details: According to its official website, Google Research publishes findings, releases open-source software, and applies research results within Google products and services as well as within the wider scientific community.

explainer.lead: Google Research is Google's research division, also known as Research at Google. It connects research with practical use by publishing findings, releasing open-source software, and applying results in Google products and services and the wider scientific community.

tiers.eli5: Google Research is like a workshop inside Google where people investigate ideas and share what they discover. Their work can become papers or software that others can use, and some results can help improve Google's products and services.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers can encounter its work through published findings, open-source software, or research applied within Google products and services. A practical pitfall is treating Google Research as one software product rather than a division whose outputs take several forms.
tiers.paperLevel: Google Research is the research division of Google, a subsidiary of Alphabet Inc., and is also known as Research at Google.
